q1.title: A Nifty 500 SIP lost money in 29% of one-year windows, 7% of five-year ones and none of the ten-year ones
q1.sub: Share of SIPs started each month since January 1995 that ended below the money put in, below the same money in fixed deposits, or below inflation. ₹10,000 on the first trading day of each month, after a 0.2% a year index-fund cost, before tax.
q1.read: Each dot is a share of start months. Read across a row: the longer the SIP ran, the rarer each kind of failure. The beat-the-FD line falls slowest, because a deposit is a tougher bar than zero.
q1.source: NSE total-return indices (Nifty 500 from 1995); RBI deposit rates; tipsheet calculations
q1.note: Evidence: measured. A count or distribution over the full sample.

q1_tax.title: After today's tax on redemption, 16% of five-year SIPs ended behind an FD, against 16% before tax
q1_tax.sub: The same windows, with long-term gains above ₹1.25 lakh taxed at 12.5% and short-term gains at 20% when the SIP is cashed in. The FD is taxed every year at 30% plus cess.
q1_tax.read: The grey bar is before tax, the coloured bar after. Tax matters most at short horizons, where more of the SIP is short-term.
q1_tax.source: NSE total-return indices (Nifty 500 from 1995); RBI deposit rates; tipsheet calculations
q1_tax.note: Evidence: measured. A count or distribution over the full sample.

q1_menu.title: Over five years, the risk of ending behind an FD depended on what the SIP bought
q1_menu.sub: Share of five-year SIPs started each month from April 2005 that ended behind the same money in FDs, by what they bought.
q1_menu.read: One bar per asset. Longer bars mean more five-year windows in which the SIP did worse than a fixed deposit.
q1_menu.source: NSE total-return indices, NSE 5-year G-sec index, domestic gold price; RBI deposit rates; tipsheet calculations

series.label: Behind an FD at five years

q1_menu.note: Evidence: measured. A count or distribution over the full sample.

q2.title: The typical ten-year Nifty 500 SIP returned 14.6% a year, but one in twenty returned under 9.8%
q2.sub: Spread of SIP returns (XIRR) across start months since 1995, by how long the SIP ran. The dashed line is the 12% most SIP calculators assume. ₹10,000 on the first trading day of each month, after a 0.2% a year index-fund cost, before tax.
q2.read: For each horizon, the dot is the middle result, the thick bar the middle half and the thin line the 5th to 95th percentile. The spread narrows sharply with time, but never closes.
q2.source: NSE total-return indices (Nifty 500 from 1995); RBI deposit rates; tipsheet calculations
q2.note: Evidence: measured. A count or distribution over the full sample.

q2_rupees.title: ₹10,000 a month for 20 years (₹24 lakh in all) became ₹1.30 crore in the typical Nifty 500 SIP
q2_rupees.sub: What the SIP was worth at the end, for a bad start (5th percentile), the typical start and a lucky start, beside the money put in. Rupees of the day.
q2_rupees.read: Grey is what you put in. The three coloured dots show how much the ending depended on when you happened to start.
q2_rupees.source: NSE total-return indices (Nifty 500 from 1995); RBI deposit rates; tipsheet calculations
q2_rupees.note: Evidence: measured. A count or distribution over the full sample.

q3.title: After inflation, the typical ten-year Nifty 500 SIP returned 8.3% a year, not 14.6%
q3.sub: Median SIP return by horizon, before and after inflation (each instalment and the final value deflated by all-India CPI to the start month).
q3.read: Grey is the return you see on a statement; colour is what it bought. The gap is roughly the inflation rate.
q3.source: NSE total-return indices (Nifty 500 from 1995); RBI deposit rates; tipsheet calculations; CPI (MoSPI)
q3.note: Evidence: measured. A count or distribution over the full sample.

q3_fd.title: Since January 1995, an FD after tax lost 0.7 points a year to inflation; the Nifty 500 beat it by 5.2% a year
q3_fd.sub: Annual return over the whole period, before and after inflation: the Nifty 500 total-return index and a fixed deposit rolled at banks' 1-3 year rate, interest taxed at 30% plus cess.
q3_fd.read: Each pair of bars is one investment. The coloured bar is what it earned after inflation; the FD's is below zero.
q3_fd.source: NSE total-return indices (Nifty 500 from 1995); RBI deposit rates; tipsheet calculations; CPI (MoSPI)
q3_fd.note: Evidence: measured. A count or distribution over the full sample.

q4.title: What a SIP bought set both its typical return and its bad case
q4.sub: Ten-year SIPs started each month from April 2005: the median return (up) against the 5th-percentile return (across), one point per asset. Mid- and small-cap history before 2016 is back-calculated by NSE.
q4.read: Up is better on average; right is better in a bad decade. No asset is top-right on its own, which is the case for mixing them.
q4.source: NSE total-return indices, NSE 5-year G-sec index, domestic gold price; RBI deposit rates; tipsheet calculations
q4.note: Evidence: measured. A count or distribution over the full sample.

q4_pain.title: Small caps fell deepest below the money put in; government bonds barely dipped
q4_pain.sub: Ten-year SIPs from April 2005: the deepest the month-end value fell below the money put in, in the worst start month, by asset.
q4_pain.read: Each bar is the worst moment a SIP in that asset went through, as a share of the money put in so far.
q4_pain.source: NSE total-return indices, NSE 5-year G-sec index, domestic gold price; RBI deposit rates; tipsheet calculations

q5.title: Over ten years, a 60/20/20 SIP gave up ₹1.4 lakh in the typical case to gain ₹0.2 lakh in a bad one
q5.sub: 60% Nifty 500, 20% government bonds, 20% gold, rebalanced each April, against an all-Nifty 500 SIP over the same months (starts from April 2005): the typical final value given up, and the bad-case (5th percentile) final value gained.
q5.read: For each horizon, compare the two bars. Where 'gained in a bad case' is longer, diversifying paid for itself; where 'given up' is longer, it cost more than it protected.
q5.source: NSE total-return indices, NSE 5-year G-sec index, domestic gold price; RBI deposit rates; tipsheet calculations

series.label: Given up in the typical case

q5_menu.sub: Ten-year SIPs from April 2005: median and 5th-percentile return of each portfolio.

q6.read: Each bar is one start month. Above zero, rebalancing helped. At least nine in ten bars are above zero.

q7.title: From 5 to 20 years, the spread of yearly returns shrank from 41 points to 3.5 points
q7.sub: Nifty 500 SIPs since 1995: the 5th and 95th percentile return a year, by horizon.
q7.read: The two dots for each horizon bracket nine in ten outcomes. They squeeze together as the SIP runs longer.

q7.note: Evidence: measured. A count or distribution over the full sample.

q7_mult.title: But in rupees the gap did not shrink: at 20 years the final value ran from 4.2 to 6.4 times the money put in
q7_mult.sub: Nifty 500 SIPs since 1995: the 5th and 95th percentile final value, as a multiple of the money put in, by horizon.
q7_mult.read: A small difference in yearly return, compounded over 20 years, is a large difference in rupees.
q7_mult.source: NSE total-return indices (Nifty 500 from 1995); RBI deposit rates; tipsheet calculations
q7_mult.note: Evidence: measured. A count or distribution over the full sample.

q8.title: The start year mattered enormously: the median ten-year return ranged from 9.3% to 26.5%
q8.sub: Median ten-year Nifty 500 SIP return for start months in each calendar year. Years before 1999 rest on a probably back-calculated index.
q8.read: Each bar is one start year. Nobody could have known in advance which bar they were standing on.
q8.source: NSE total-return indices (Nifty 500 from 1995); RBI deposit rates; tipsheet calculations
q8.note: Evidence: measured. A count or distribution over the full sample.

q8_bands.title: Starting near a market high made little difference: 13.6% against 14.9% for starts more than 10% below it
q8_bands.sub: Ten-year Nifty 500 SIP returns by how far the market was below its previous high in the start month.
q8_bands.read: Each row shows the median (dot) and the 5th to 95th percentile range. The rows overlap almost completely.

q9_years.title: In a 15-year SIP, the first five years' instalments made up 55% of the final value; the last five, 14%
q9_years.sub: Share of a 15-year Nifty 500 SIP's final value that came from each year's instalments (median across start months since 1995).
q9_years.read: Each bar is one year of instalments. Early money had the longest to compound, so it ended up doing most of the work.
q9_years.source: NSE total-return indices (Nifty 500 from 1995); RBI deposit rates; tipsheet calculations
q9_years.note: Evidence: measured. A count or distribution over the full sample.

q9_glide.title: Moving to FDs over the last three years ended ahead in only 19% of 15-year SIPs, and lowered even the bad case
q9_glide.sub: 15-year Nifty 500 SIPs since 1995: final value if the SIP stayed invested, against switching the corpus to FDs in 36 (or 12) equal monthly steps and paying the last instalments into FDs. Equity before tax; FD interest taxed.
q9_glide.read: For each choice: the dot is the typical final value, the line runs from the bad case (5th percentile) to the median. Staying put was better in both.
q9_glide.source: NSE total-return indices (Nifty 500 from 1995); RBI deposit rates; tipsheet calculations

q16_mechanism.title: Why a bad start helped: 18% of the money went in while the SIP was red, but it bought 30% of the units

q16_mechanism.read: Money put in during the bad months bought units cheaply. Those units are worth the same as any other at the end, so they punch above their weight.

q20.title: Investors' SIP money earned 11.2% a year, against 11.3% for money growing at the same trend: no sign of bad timing
q20.sub: AMFI's monthly SIP inflows, April 2016 to September 2026, as if invested in the Nifty 500 total-return index, against a steady SIP, a SIP growing at the inflows' own trend (23% a year), and the index itself. Before tax and costs.
q20.read: A steady SIP is the wrong yardstick: inflows grew every year, so more money naturally went in later, at higher prices. Against the fair yardstick the gap all but disappears.
q20.source: AMFI monthly SIP data (via India Data Hub); NSE; tipsheet calculations
q20.note: Evidence: measured. A count or distribution over the full sample.
